answer.justification: The patient's clinical presentation (foul-smelling diarrhea after antibiotic use) and culture results (gram-positive, anaerobic rods) are highly suggestive of Clostridioides difficile infection. C. difficile forms highly resistant spores. While alcohol, iodine, and quaternary amines are ineffective against spores, chlorine-based solutions (such as sodium hypochlorite) are sporicidal and are the standard for environmental decontamination to prevent the transmission of C. difficile.
